title: Goodman as perfectionist, as improviser, and Artie Shaw's tone
summary: Goodman was a perfectionist with a glare; Stewart thinks he was not the King of Swing and preferred Artie Shaw's tone and harmony.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: What kind of a person did you see Goodman to be over the years, because you worked with him recently, too.

Well, yes. Recently is my second time around with him since then. Of course, I've found that Benny is a -- you might say he's a taskmaster, what I mean. He's a perfectionist. He wants everything just right. Of course,

you probably heard the story that he's a hard man to work with and to get by. Well, I did notice amongst the fellas who I was working along with with Benny, the times that I was with him, that he would really give some of the fellas a hard time, especially if they played some notes that Benny didn't like and as I said, Benny was a perfectionist, you know, he wanted things just right. If things weren't right, you would know it because they used to call Benny "The Ray," , you know. He wore glasses most of the time and he would look over if something was wrong, he'd look over at you and you'd know it.
That ray was on you, so you'd know there's something wrong.
What did you think of him as an improvisor?

Oh, he was very good at improvising and his musicianship, you might say, was great. He was great with that clarinet and even when I went back with him the second time around, he's still blowing real good, yeah.
Do you think he was overrated?
You really think he was the King of Swing?
I don't think he was the king, no.

I don't think he was the king, as they called him, because personally -- nothing against him as a person, or anything like that -- but if I must say so, I enjoyed listening to Artie Shaw much better than at times listening to Benny, although Benny was great. I enjoyed listening and playing with Benny, of course. But it was something about Artie Shaw's playing that I enjoy even a little bit more.
Do you think it was because Shaw was more sophistically harmonically?
Yes. And his tone, I enjoyed his tone moreso.
